classification.difficultyReason: Distinguish dependence on x or y, then compare equilibrium and gradient signs.

content.prompt: Which slope field (A, B, C, or D) corresponds to $y'=-2-y$?

spec.description: Four ungridded coordinate slope fields in a two-by-two comparison: A and B above C and D. Each has all 81 direction segments at integer coordinates from −5 to 3 on both axes. Option labels and nonzero integer tick labels are retained.
spec.mathematics: A: slope x+2; B: slope −x−2; C: slope y+2; D: slope −y−2. Equal-length segments are normalised to preserve their gradients and relative steepness.
spec.answerVisibility: All four fields are permanent student-visible options; no correct-option marking.

answer.worked:
The gradient depends only on $y$, so segments in each horizontal row have the same gradient. This eliminates A and B.

Setting $y'=0$ gives $y=-2$, so the field has horizontal segments along $y=-2$. Both C and D have this property.

For $y>-2$, $y'=-2-y<0$; for $y<-2$, $y'>0$. D has negative gradients above $y=-2$ and positive gradients below it.

Correct answer: D.
